title: Clear the weeds
intro: Well, look at you! Tobias said you'd come.
This place is more weed than farm. Pull a few of those weeds and let's see some soil.
outro: There's the old dirt! Tobias always said it was the best in the valley.
Here, a little something to buy seeds with.

title: Your first harvest
intro: Pick a seed from the tray and tap the soil. Radishes are ready before you can say 'pie'.
Bring in five crops and I'll show you how to sell them.
outro: Look at that haul! They go in your barn until you sell them.

title: Fill the shipping crate
intro: See the crate in your barn? Anything you put in there, I'll buy. Not top price, mind, but it's instant.
Ship five crops.
outro: Pleasure doing business! Now, folks in town have been asking for fresh food.
I'll pin their orders on your request board. Orders pay much better than the crate.

title: Goldie's carrot order
intro: I've pinned an order of my own on the board. Four carrots for my famous carrot cake.
Bring them and I'll pay you properly.
outro: Perfect carrots! Oh, and Bruno the carpenter wants a word about that sorry gate of yours.
I think he left you a note.

title: Rebuild the gate
intro: So you're Tobias's kin. Good to meet you.
Bring me 4 wood, 3 stone and 60 coins, and I'll have that gate rebuilt overnight. Branches give wood; rocks give stone.
outro: That's everything. Leave it with me. Check your mailbox in the morning.

title: The grumpy miller
intro: Don't need help. Don't need a farmer. Don't need anything.
Fine. If you're so keen, bring me 10 wheat. Then we'll talk.
outro: Hm. Good wheat. Tobias's soil, no doubt.
The mill's wheel is jammed solid and the path is choked with old stumps. Bruno can tell you about those.

title: Old stumps
intro: Rufus sent you? Ha! Those stumps by the mill path have been there since before I was born.
Buy a saw from Goldie's store in Town, then cut two stumps. We'll need the wood anyway.
outro: Nice work. That wood will go straight into the mill.

title: Restore the mill
intro: So you're serious. All right.
The mill needs three things: timber and stone for the frame, wheat to test the stones, and coins for a new wheel. Find the project in Town.
outro: Listen. Hear that? No, you don't. Not yet. Bruno's fitting the wheel tonight.
Come back tomorrow.

title: First flour
intro: Wheel's turning. Now let's see if you can use it.
Tap the mill behind your farm, put in wheat, and bring me 3 bags of flour.
outro: Fine flour. Finest in twenty years. Don't tell anyone I said so.
Tobias will want to hear about this.

title: The nervous baker
intro: Oh! Hello. Sorry. I'm Pip. I run the bakery. Well, I used to. Well, I still do, just... without flour.
Rufus says your flour is the real thing. Could you bring me 6 bags? I'll pay. I'll overpay. Is overpaying weird?
outro: It's perfect. It's so perfect I might cry. I'm not crying. It's flour in my eyes.
Now if only the market square wasn't such a ruin. Bruno says the stalls could be saved...

title: Rebuild the market square
intro: The old market square! I've been waiting years for someone to ask.
Mend the stalls, fill them for opening day, then string up some bunting. You'll find the project in Town.
outro: Stalls are up, bunting's flying. I'll put the finishing touches on tonight.
Bramblewick has a market again. Check your mail in the morning.

title: Opening day
intro: Opening day! Opening day! Everyone's coming and I have nothing on my table.
Berry pastries. Two of them. Flour and jam from your bakery. You do have a bakery? Bruno can build one. Please hurry. Not too much. Some hurry.
outro: They sold out in four minutes. FOUR. Goldie bought one and then bought the other one.
Oh, and some strange man with a cart asked about you. Very big hat. Very big smile.

title: A most remarkable cart
intro: Ziggy Marlowe, purveyor of the rare, the wondrous and the very slightly questionable! At your service.
My cart rolls into Bramblewick every third day. Seeds from beyond the mountains, gold from who-knows-where. Have a browse in Town. Buy just one thing and we're friends for life.
outro: A customer of taste! I knew it the moment I saw your boots.
Do you know a Dr. Quill? Botanist. Terribly clever. She's been asking about Tobias's old seed collection...

title: The botanist
intro: Dr. Hazel Quill. Botanist. You must be the great-niece, or great-nephew, or whatever Tobias calls you. He was vague. He's always vague.
Tobias left me his almanac. Half the pages are blank and the other half are covered in jam. I need specimens.
Grow ten different crops and I'll record each one in the Almanac. You'll find it in Town.
outro: Ten species, all healthy, all correctly labelled by me. Satisfactory. More than satisfactory.
There's a child who keeps following me around with a dog. She says she's an inventor. Could you... deal with that?

title: Juniper's invention
intro: Hi! I'm Juniper and this is Moss. Moss, say hi. He's saying hi.
I'm building the world's first Automatic Carrot Launcher. Moss LOVES carrots. Like, more than me, probably.
I need 30 carrots for testing and 10 wood for the launcher. Please? Moss is doing his please face.
outro: IT WORKS! Well, it launched one carrot into the river. But Moss got the other twenty-nine!
Moss likes your farm. He wants to visit. He's going to visit whether you say yes or not, but saying yes is nicer.

title: A true expert
intro: A good farmer grows everything. A great farmer knows one crop better than anyone alive.
Harvest any single crop fifty times and you'll earn a mastery star. The Almanac keeps count.
outro: Fifty harvests. You know that crop's moods better than your own now. I approve.
Tobias marked one page of the almanac with a pressed sunflower. I think I know what it means.

title: Tobias's heirloom
intro: The pressed-sunflower page. Tobias wrote: 'Sunflowers for the sun, pumpkins for the soil, and the rest is patience.'
It's a recipe for soil. The soil a golden melon needs. Bring me ten of each and I'll prove it.
outro: It's true. Tobias was growing golden melons here forty years ago, and nobody believed him. Including me.
I'm writing to him tonight. I suspect he'll want to see this for himself.

title: The harvest festival
intro: Tobias is coming home! Tobias! I haven't slept. I've made a list. The list has lists.
We're throwing the first harvest festival in twenty years, and the whole valley's invited.
Bunting and tables, a proper feast, and a prize table worth the name. Find the festival in Town projects.
outro: Look at it. The square's full. Bruno's crying. He says it's sawdust. There's no sawdust.
Hazel wants a word. Something about seeds. She looks almost excited, which is frightening.

title: Something golden
intro: These are Tobias's golden melon seeds. Forty years old. I've kept them in a tin marked 'DO NOT EAT', mostly for Juniper.
The soil's ready, thanks to you. Plant one and grow it. It takes two whole days. Patience was always Tobias's best crop.
outro: Gold. Actually gold. I'm drawing it on the first page of the Almanac, as promised.
Hold on to it. I believe someone's coming up the road.

title: The golden harvest
intro: Well now. Look at this place.
I left a field of weeds and a valley with its lights off. And here's a mill turning, and a market, and bunting, and a dog asleep in my carrots.
Hazel tells me you grew something golden. May I see it?
outro: Forty years I told them golden melons would grow here. Forty years, and you did it in one season.
This farm was never mine to keep, sprout. It was mine to hand on. And I couldn't have handed it to better hands.
Now. Goldie promised me a pie, and I intend to collect. Come on, the whole valley's waiting.

title: The old creek dock
intro: The creek dock? I know it. Tobias and I built that the summer I was apprenticing. He held the hammer like a spoon.
It needs new pilings and decking. Bring me 40 wood, 15 stone and 5,000 coins for the ironwork, and I'll have it standing in a day.
outro: There. Solid as the mill. Solider. Don't tell Rufus.
Somebody's already watching from the houseboat on the far bank. That'll be Nell. Go say hello. Bring patience.

title: The river-keeper
intro: So. You're the one fixing things. Tobias's sprout.
You want to cross, you learn the creek first. Cast your line, wait for the bobber to dip, then pull. Not before. Not after. Then.
Catch me three fish. Any three. The Creek's in Town now that there's a dock to stand on.
outro: Three fish and you didn't fall in. That's better than your great-uncle managed.
Every fish you land the first time, I'll write you a note about it. Somebody ought to know who lives down there.

title: Neighbours
intro: The creek's not one place. It's a morning place and an evening place and a place that only wakes up after dark.
Find me five different kinds. Come down at different hours. The char won't wait for you to finish breakfast.
outro: Five neighbours. You're starting to know the street.
Rufus was up at the mill race this morning, staring at the water. He used to come down here every day, you know. Before.

title: A peace offering
intro: You've been fishing with Nell Brightwater. Don't look at me like that, I can see the creek from the mill.
The year of the flood I shut the race to save the town, and the water went to her side. Her mother's boat went with it. We haven't spoken since.
Edie, my wife, used to make a trout pie. Nell loved it. Bring me 5 brook trout and 5 flour. I'll bake it. Then I'll... carry it over. Probably.
outro: She ate two slices. Didn't say anything for a long time. Then she said the crust was too thick.
Edie's crust was always too thick. Nell used to say that every time. ...It was a good day. Don't make a thing of it.

title: Nell's ferry
intro: Rufus brought pie. Twenty years and he brings pie. I didn't know what to do with my hands.
Anyway. The ferry. It's been leaking since the flood and I've been too stubborn to ask anyone for anything.
I'm asking. 30 wood for the hull, 10 cotton for a new sail, and 5 honey to seal the seams. Old trick.
outro: Floats. Floats and doesn't leak. I'd forgotten what that sounds like. Quiet.
Tobias wants to cross tomorrow. Says there's something of his still standing on the far bank. I'll take him. Slowly. Over the deep bit.
